answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every new identity to escrow a steadily rising copper bond and to present a relic of prior unpaid work that only matures after a timber seasoning period. The bond is slashed if the account is caught cloning or stuffing attestations, and the seasoning clock does not transfer when keys are copied. Standing up a thousand fake agents therefore means locking a thousand copper stakes and waiting through a thousand independent timber delays, which quickly outruns the expected reward from packing the voter roll.
